acciones: dispels Wind-Dampness and unblocks the channels and collaterals

eczema
uso_historico: Recorded in the Ben Cao Gang Mu Shi Yi (Qing dynasty), which describes its ability to "widely open the twelve channels" and treat water retention and obstruction. Its name literally means "all roads connect."
precauciones: Contraindicated during pregnancy (risk of miscarriage), with heavy menstrual bleeding, and with active bleeding; use caution in Yin deficiency without stasis.

acciones: clears Heat and resolves Fire toxicity
cools the Blood and stops bleeding
resolves Damp-Heat in the Large Intestine
indicaciones_tradicionales: Damp-Heat dysentery with tenesmus and stools containing blood and mucus
Heat-type diarrhea
boils, carbuncles, and inflamed sores (internal and external use, fresh and crushed)
wasp stings and snakebites (external use)
uterine bleeding due to Heat in the Blood
blood in the stool and bleeding hemorrhoids
painful or bloody urination
Damp-Heat vaginal discharge
uso_historico: Recorded in the materia medica literature since Tao Hongjing's Ben Cao Jing Ji Zhu. It has traditionally been used as both a food and a medicinal plant, especially for dysentery and, fresh and crushed, for ulcers and stings.
precauciones: Contraindicated during pregnancy (it may stimulate the uterus) and in Spleen and Stomach deficiency with Cold and loose stools. Contains oxalates; use caution in people with oxalate kidney stones.

acciones: moistens the Lung and stops cough
clears Heart Fire and eliminates irritability

dry mouth and throat, thirst
Stomach Yin deficiency with a dry tongue
irritability and insomnia due to Heat in the Heart
palpitations
constipation due to dryness of fluids
uso_historico: Recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing as a superior-grade medicine. It is the chief herb, at a high dose, in Zhang Zhongjing's Mai Men Dong Tang for nourishing Lung and Stomach Yin; it is also part of Sheng Mai San.
precauciones: Avoid in Spleen and Stomach deficiency Cold with loose stools, accumulation of Phlegm-Dampness, and acute cough due to Wind-Cold.

acciones: clears Wind-Heat from the Liver channel and brightens the eyes
indicaciones_tradicionales: headache due to Wind-Heat, especially temporal or frontal
pain and heaviness of the head
red, swollen, painful eyes with tearing
blurred vision and spots before the eyes
dizziness due to Wind-Heat
stiffness and pain of the limbs due to Wind-Dampness
uso_historico: Recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing as a superior-grade herb. It is classically used for headache and eye disorders due to Wind-Heat, and in Yi Qi Cong Ming Tang for the eyes and ears.
precauciones: Use caution in Yin or Blood deficiency and in Spleen and Stomach Qi deficiency.
nota: Not to be confused with the fruit of Vitex agnus-castus (chasteberry, used in Western herbalism for hormonal disorders). It was assumed to be man jing zi, the Vitex fruit of the Chinese materia medica.

categoria_mtc: clears Heat and cools the Blood
acciones: clears Heat and cools the Blood

uso_historico: Recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing as a middle-grade herb. It is a component of classical formulas such as Liu Wei Di Huang Wan, Gui Zhi Fu Ling Wan, and Da Huang Mu Dan Tang.
precauciones: Contraindicated during pregnancy, in bleeding due to Cold, in excessive menstruation without Heat, and in Stomach deficiency with Cold.
etiquetas: tree peony root bark (moutan root bark)

acciones: relaxes the tendons and unblocks the channels
harmonizes the Stomach and transforms Dampness

vomiting, diarrhea, and cramps due to turbid Dampness
uso_historico: Recorded in the Ming Yi Bie Lu. It is especially valued for muscle stiffness and cramps, often combined with bai shao.
precauciones: Avoid in internal Heat with scanty, dark urine, in gastric hyperacidity, and in low back or knee weakness due to deficiency of Essence, Blood, or Yin. Excessive use may damage the teeth and bones.

latin: Ostrea gigas Thunb., Ostrea rivularis Gould y otras especies de Ostrea (Concha Ostreae)

heartburn and stomach pain (calcined form)
uso_historico: Recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing as a superior-grade substance. It is classically combined with Long Gu to settle the spirit and anchor Yang, for example in Gui Zhi Jia Long Gu Mu Li Tang.
precauciones: Prolonged use may cause constipation or indigestion. Avoid with shellfish allergy. Traditionally avoided in deficiency-Cold patterns without Heat. As a source of calcium, it may interfere with the absorption of some drugs (e.g., tetracyclines).

categoria_mtc: releases the exterior: pungent and cool (disperses Wind-Heat)
acciones: disperses Wind-Heat and benefits the throat

sore, swollen throat
measles with a rash that fails to erupt
mumps
itchy skin rashes
boils, carbuncles, and swellings due to Heat toxins
constipation due to Heat
uso_historico: Recorded in the Ming Yi Bie Lu. It is a classic component of Wind-Heat formulas such as Yin Qiao San, used especially for sore throat and to vent measles.
precauciones: Use with caution in Qi deficiency and diarrhea, or when there is no excess Heat. Contraindicated in open sores that have already suppurated. Use caution during pregnancy. May enhance antidiabetic drugs (risk of hypoglycemia).

categoria_mtc: invigorates the Blood and eliminates stasis
acciones: invigorates the Blood and disperses stasis
promotes urination and relieves painful urination (lin syndrome)

menstrual irregularities
pain from trauma

painful or bloody urination (lin syndrome)
joint pain due to Cold-Dampness (bi syndrome)
uso_historico: It appears in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing, where it is recommended for atrophy and bi syndrome (painful obstruction) due to Cold-Dampness. It is traditionally used as an herb that directs a formula's action to the lower body.
precauciones: Contraindicated during pregnancy and with excessive menstruation. Use with caution in diarrhea due to Spleen deficiency, spermatorrhea, and sinking of Middle Jiao Qi.

indicaciones_tradicionales: premature graying
blurred vision and reduced visual acuity due to Liver and Kidney Yin deficiency

night sweats and heat in the palms and soles due to Yin deficiency
menopausal symptoms due to Yin deficiency
uso_historico: Recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing as a superior-grade medicine, non-toxic and suitable for long-term use. It is classically combined with Han Lian Cao in Er Zhi Wan to nourish Liver and Kidney Yin.
precauciones: Avoid in Spleen and Stomach deficiency with Cold-type diarrhea; use with caution in Yang deficiency. Avoid with hypersensitivity to plants of the Oleaceae family.

latin: Herba Taraxaci (Taraxacum mongolicum Hand.-Mazz.; T. officinale)

insufficient lactation
uso_historico: First recorded in the Xin Xiu Ben Cao (Tang dynasty). It is traditionally considered the chief herb for breast abscesses, used both internally and as a poultice.
precauciones: An overdose may cause mild diarrhea. Contraindicated in Yin-type lesions (without redness or pain) and in Middle Jiao deficiency. May cause allergic reactions (itching, hives), especially in people allergic to the Asteraceae family. Possible interaction with quinolone antibiotics, diuretics, and lithium.

acciones: relaxes the tendons and unblocks the collaterals

uso_historico: Recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing as a middle-grade herb for pathogenic Cold-Heat Qi and Wind obstruction syndrome (feng bi). It is used in formulas such as Qin Jiao Bie Jia San for deficiency fever.
precauciones: Avoid during pregnancy, in chronic diarrhea or loose stools, excessive urination, deficiency Cold in the lower body, and severe Yin deficiency.

latin: Citrus reticulata Blanco (Citri Reticulatae Viride Pericarpium)

uso_historico: Recorded in the Ben Cao Tu Jing (Song dynasty). It is considered stronger than chen pi and especially useful for pain due to Liver Qi stagnation.
precauciones: Contraindicated with excessive sweating. Use caution in Qi deficiency; prolonged use and high doses are not recommended.
etiquetas: blue citrus peel (tangerine green fruit rind)

latin: Radix Ginseng (Panax ginseng C. A. Mey.)

uso_historico: Classified as a superior herb in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing. It is the most important Qi tonic in Chinese medicine, used alone (Du Shen Tang) to rescue collapse and in formulas such as Si Jun Zi Tang.
precauciones: Contraindicated in Yin deficiency with Heat, excess Heat, and rising Liver Yang; avoid in severe hypertension. Do not combine with coffee or other stimulants. May interact with MAOIs (mania), warfarin, and antidiabetic drugs (hypoglycemia). Overuse may cause insomnia, nervousness, hypertension, and bleeding. Incompatible with Li Lu; traditionally antagonized by Lai Fu Zi and Wu Ling Zhi.

acciones: tonifies Kidney Yang and strengthens Essence (jing) and Blood

uso_historico: Recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing as a superior-class tonic. It is valued because it tonifies Yang gently and gradually without drying.
precauciones: Contraindicated in Spleen and Stomach deficiency with diarrhea, Yin deficiency with Heat or premature ejaculation, and excess Heat. May interact with sympathomimetics, MAOIs, SSRIs, and tricyclic antidepressants.

uso_historico: Recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing. The physician Qian Yi (Song dynasty) used it as the chief herb in Xie Bai San, a classic pediatric formula for cough due to Lung Heat.
precauciones: Avoid in Lung deficiency without Heat, cough due to Wind-Cold, excessive urination, and Spleen and Stomach deficiency Cold. Use with caution during pregnancy.

acciones: moves Qi and aromatically transforms Dampness

uso_historico: Recorded since the Tang dynasty (Yao Xing Lun). It is added to tonifying formulas such as Xiang Sha Liu Jun Zi Tang to keep the tonics from stagnating digestion.
precauciones: Contraindicated in Yin deficiency with Heat, Blood deficiency, and intense Fire; avoid in abdominal pain due to Fire or in diarrhea due to Summer Heat. Use caution during pregnancy. Possible interaction with anticoagulants and antiplatelet drugs.
nota: In Chinese formula products (Sun Ten style, the source of the names on these labels), 'cardamom' corresponds to sha ren (Amomum villosum), not to bai dou kou ('round cardamom') or to culinary cardamom, Elettaria cardamomum.

acciones: tonifies Spleen and Stomach Qi and Yin

uso_historico: Classified as a superior herb in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing. It is one of the three tonifying herbs in Liu Wei Di Huang Wan and has been widely used as a food-medicine for the Spleen, Lung, and Kidney.
precauciones: Do not use alone in excess, Dampness, or stagnation patterns, or in true Heat. Use caution with insulin and antidiabetic drugs because of a possible synergistic blood-sugar-lowering effect. Antagonizes Gan Sui.

uso_historico: It appears in Tang dynasty texts (Xin Xiu Ben Cao). It has traditionally been used to digest meat and fats, as in Bao He Wan, and for postpartum Blood stasis; in modern practice it is also used for cardiovascular problems.
precauciones: Avoid in Spleen and Stomach deficiency without food stagnation; use with caution in acid regurgitation and peptic ulcer. High doses are contraindicated during pregnancy. May enhance digoxin and cardiovascular/antihypertensive drugs.

uso_historico: Mentioned in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing. It is one of the 'three tonifying herbs' in the formula Liu Wei Di Huang Wan and was traditionally used to strengthen vigor and prolong life, as well as in large doses for collapse with profuse sweating.
precauciones: Contraindicated with exuberant Ming Men Fire, Damp-Heat, or painful urination due to Heat in the Bladder. Antagonizes Jie Geng, Fang Feng, and Fang Ji. May have additive effects with diuretics.
etiquetas: cornus fruit without seeds (Asiatic dogwood fruit)

uso_historico: First recorded in the Yao Xing Lun (Tang era). It was prepared by fermenting flour with various herbs; besides its digestive use, it is added to pills containing minerals to make them easier to digest.
precauciones: Contraindicated in Stomach Yin deficiency and Stomach Fire. Use with caution during pregnancy.
nota: It is not a whole plant: 'shen-chu' is the Wade-Giles transcription of shen qu, a fermented mass of flour and herbs; the 'whole plant' description on the label is inaccurate.

uso_historico: Di huang appears in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing as a superior-grade herb. The distinction between the raw root (sheng di huang, which cools the Blood) and the prepared root (shu di huang, which tonifies Blood and Yin) was established in later materia medica.
precauciones: Contraindicated in Spleen deficiency with Dampness, abdominal distension, and loose stools. May cause mild diarrhea or digestive discomfort. Traditionally, use caution with iron preparations.
nota: The label does not indicate whether this is the raw root (sheng di huang) or the prepared root (shu di huang, 熟地黄, warm and sweet, which tonifies Blood and Kidney Yin). The raw form was assumed because no preparation was specified.

acciones: releases the exterior and disperses Cold

uso_historico: Recorded in the Ming Yi Bie Lu (dried ginger, Gan Jiang, already appears in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing). Traditionally called 'the sacred herb for vomiting' and widely used in Shang Han Lun formulas such as Gui Zhi Tang.
precauciones: Contraindicated in spontaneous sweating due to exterior deficiency, Lung Heat, vomiting due to Stomach Heat, and Yin deficiency with Heat. In high doses it may enhance anticoagulants.
nota: The label says 'ginger rhizome' without specifying; it is assumed to be Sheng Jiang (fresh ginger). If it is dried ginger (Gan Jiang), its nature is hot and its main action is to warm the Middle Jiao and rescue Yang.

joint pain due to Wind-Dampness
sore throat
uso_historico: Recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing as chang pu. It is considered the chief herb for opening the orifices and is often combined with yuan zhi for forgetfulness and mental confusion due to Phlegm.
precauciones: Use with caution in Yin deficiency with Heat and in Blood deficiency; avoid with vomiting of blood and excessive sweating. Avoid prolonged use or high doses. The species Acorus calamus contains beta-asarone, which is considered potentially toxic.
nota: Acorus tatarinowii (shi chang pu), the standard species in TCM, is assumed; A. calamus (shui chang pu) is a less commonly used substitute.

latin: Haliotis diversicolor Reeve y otras especies de Haliotis (Concha Haliotidis)

uso_historico: First appears in the Ming Yi Bie Lu as a superior-grade substance. Its name literally means "stone that decides clarity," reflecting its classical reputation for treating eye disorders and restoring vision.
precauciones: Contraindicated in Spleen and Stomach deficiency Cold and when there is no pattern of Liver Yang or Liver Fire. Avoid with shellfish allergy. It is traditionally said not to combine well with Xuan Fu Hua.

precauciones: Avoid in patterns of excess Heat or Phlegm-Fire and in severe diarrhea. Avoid with allergy to plants of the Rhamnaceae family. May enhance sedatives.
nota: "Jujuba seed" is identified as suan zao ren (spiny jujube seed), not the da zao fruit.

acciones: clears Lung Heat, transforms Phlegm, and moistens Dryness

uso_historico: The root of gua lou (gua lou gen) appears in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing as a middle-grade herb. Traditionally it is one of the chief herbs for the thirst of xiao ke syndrome (wasting).
precauciones: Use caution in deficiency Cold and diarrhea due to Spleen and Stomach deficiency. Contraindicated during pregnancy (it may induce miscarriage). Traditionally incompatible with wu tou (Aconitum). High doses may cause allergic reactions.

acciones: extinguishes Liver Wind and stops spasms

joint and limb pain due to Wind-Dampness
uso_historico: Recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing (as Chi Jian) as a superior herb. It is one of the chief herbs for dizziness and headache, used in Tian Ma Gou Teng Yin and in Ban Xia Bai Zhu Tian Ma Tang.
precauciones: Considered safe at normal doses. Use with sedatives (barbiturates, benzodiazepines, antihistamines, narcotic pain relievers) may prolong sedation. Use with caution in severe Blood deficiency.

acciones: clears Lung Heat and drains Fire
moistens Dryness, generates fluids, and transforms Phlegm

uso_historico: It appears in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing as a superior-class tonic. It is traditionally combined with mai men dong for dry cough due to Lung and Kidney Yin deficiency.
precauciones: Avoid in Spleen deficiency with Cold, diarrhea, and poor appetite, and in cough due to Wind-Cold.
etiquetas: asparagus root tuber (Chinese asparagus root tuber)

uso_historico: Classified as a superior-category herb in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing. It has traditionally been used as a balanced tonic for Kidney Yin and Yang, for example in Wu Zi Yan Zong Wan for infertility and sexual weakness.
precauciones: Contraindicated in Yin deficiency with Heat, constipation, scanty dark urine, and persistent erection (priapism).

acciones: restrains Lung Qi and stops cough
tonifies the Kidney and secures the Essence
calms the spirit and nourishes the Heart

insomnia, palpitations, and excessive dreaming
poor memory
uso_historico: Recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing as a superior-grade herb. Its name ('five-flavor fruit') refers to the fact that it combines all five flavors; it is used in classical formulas such as Sheng Mai San and Xiao Qing Long Tang.
precauciones: Contraindicated with unresolved external pathogens, excess internal Heat, and cough or rashes in their early stage. May cause heartburn. Induces liver enzymes (CYP3A4) and may alter levels of drugs such as tacrolimus or cyclosporine.

pinyin: xi ming (su bai jiang; comercializado como bai jiang cao)
acciones: clears the Liver and brightens the eyes
harmonizes the Middle Jiao and drains Dampness
indicaciones_tradicionales: red, swollen, painful eyes

uso_historico: The seeds (xi ming zi) appear in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing. In central and southeastern China, Thlaspi arvense has often been sold as 'bai jiang cao,' an herb for intestinal abscesses and toxic sores whose authentic species is Patrinia.
precauciones: By analogy with bai jiang cao: avoid in abdominal pain due to Cold and in Spleen and Stomach deficiency with diarrhea; use with caution during pregnancy. Specific toxicity data are limited.
nota: Thlaspi arvense (xi ming / su bai jiang) is used as a regional substitute for bai jiang cao (败酱草, Patrinia scabiosifolia / P. villosa). The properties listed are those of Thlaspi according to the Chinese Pharmacopoeia (pungent, slightly cool); Patrinia is bitter and pungent, slightly cold, and also invigorates the Blood.

chest tightness and epigastric distension
disharmony between the Liver and Spleen with indigestion
irregular menstruation
menstrual cramps
premenstrual breast distension and pain
abdominal pain due to Qi stagnation
uso_historico: It appears in the Ming Yi Bie Lu (Six Dynasties period). Li Shi Zhen called it 'the commander of gynecological disorders,' and it has been widely used for Liver Qi stagnation and menstrual disorders.
precauciones: Contraindicated in Qi deficiency without stagnation, Yin deficiency with signs of Heat, and Heat in the Blood. Use with caution in constipation and during pregnancy.

latin: Semen Armeniacae Amarum (Prunus armeniaca / Prunus sibirica)
acciones: moistens the intestines and eases bowel movements
indicaciones_tradicionales: cough and wheezing due to Wind-Cold
cough due to Wind-Heat or Lung Heat (in combination)
dry cough due to Dryness
asthma with chest tightness
constipation due to intestinal dryness
uso_historico: It appears in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing (as xing he ren) as a lower-grade herb. It is a component of classical formulas for cough and asthma such as Ma Huang Tang, Ma Xing Shi Gan Tang, and Xing Su San.
precauciones: Slightly toxic: it contains amygdalin, which releases cyanide; an overdose may cause dizziness, nausea, vomiting, shortness of breath, and death. Contraindicated in cough due to Qi or Yin deficiency; use caution with diarrhea and in young children. Removing the skin and cooking it are recommended to reduce toxicity.

acciones: tonifies the Liver and Kidney and strengthens the tendons and bones
promotes Blood circulation and relieves pain
stops uterine bleeding and calms the fetus
indicaciones_tradicionales: low back and knee pain and weakness due to deficiency
joint stiffness and leg weakness
fractures, sprains, and traumatic injuries with pain and swelling
uterine bleeding during pregnancy
threatened miscarriage
excessive uterine bleeding
abscesses and sores
uso_historico: It appears in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing. Its name means 'restoring what is broken,' reflecting its traditional use for fractures and injuries to the tendons and bones, as well as for protecting pregnancy.
precauciones: Contraindicated in Yin deficiency with exuberant Fire and in Wind-Damp-Heat. Not suitable in the early stages of dysentery. Incompatible with Lei Wan.

categoria_mtc: invigorates the Blood and eliminates stasis
acciones: invigorates the Blood and eliminates stasis
unblocks the collaterals and relieves pain
astringes the Lung and calms wheezing
indicaciones_tradicionales: chest pain and tightness due to Blood stasis
dizziness
poor memory
recovery after a stroke
high cholesterol
chronic cough and wheezing
poor circulation in the limbs
uso_historico: Medicinal use of the leaf was first documented in the Ben Cao Pin Hui Jing Yao (Ming dynasty), for diarrhea and dysentery. Its modern use as an extract for brain and heart circulation came later; traditionally the seed (Bai Guo) was used more often.
precauciones: Avoid with active bleeding or bleeding disorders; use caution with anticoagulants and antiplatelet drugs; stop 1-2 weeks before surgery. Avoid with seizure disorders. Do not use raw, unprocessed leaves (toxic ginkgolic acids). Use caution during pregnancy and breastfeeding.

latin: Herba Epimedii (Epimedium brevicornum Maxim., E. sagittatum y otras especies)
acciones: tonifies Kidney Yang and strengthens libido
indicaciones_tradicionales: impotence and premature ejaculation due to Kidney Yang deficiency
infertility due to Yang deficiency
frequent urination
pain and coldness in the lower back and knees
joint pain and numbness due to Wind-Cold-Dampness
weakness or paralysis of the limbs
menopausal symptoms with Yin and Yang deficiency (e.g., menopausal hypertension)
uso_historico: It appears in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing. Its name refers to goats that became very sexually active after eating it, and it has traditionally been used as a Yang tonic for impotence and Bi pain due to Cold-Dampness.
precauciones: Contraindicated in Yin deficiency with signs of Heat and in seminal emissions due to Fire. Prolonged use may damage Yin, causing dizziness, dry mouth, thirst, and nosebleeds. Possible interactions with anticoagulants and hormonal drugs.

latin: Radix Curcumae (Curcuma wenyujin, C. longa, C. kwangsiensis o C. phaeocaulis)
categoria_mtc: invigorates the Blood and eliminates stasis
acciones: invigorates the Blood and disperses stasis
clears Heat and cools the Blood
clears the Heart and opens the orifices
benefits the gallbladder and reduces jaundice
indicaciones_tradicionales: pain in the chest, flanks, and abdomen due to Qi and Blood stagnation
menstrual cramps and painful menstruation due to Liver Qi stagnation
nosebleeds, vomiting of blood, and blood in the urine due to Heat in the Blood
agitation, anxiety, or seizures due to Phlegm-Heat obstructing the Heart
jaundice
gallstones
pain from trauma
uso_historico: It appears in the materia medica of the Tang dynasty (Yao Xing Lun / Xin Xiu Ben Cao). It was traditionally used for Qi and Blood stagnation with pain and, combined with Shi Chang Pu, for mental clouding due to Phlegm-Heat.
precauciones: Contraindicated in distension due to Qi deficiency and in Yin deficiency due to blood loss. Use with caution during pregnancy. Incompatible with Ding Xiang (clove). Possible interaction with anticoagulants.
nota: 'Curcuma root tuber' corresponds to Yu Jin (tuberous root), not to Jiang Huang (turmeric rhizome).

categoria_mtc: nourishes the Heart and calms the spirit (Shen)
acciones: calms the spirit and settles the Heart
restores communication between the Heart and Kidney
expels Phlegm and opens the Heart orifices
indicaciones_tradicionales: insomnia
palpitations with anxiety and fear
restlessness and poor memory
disorientation or mental confusion due to Phlegm obstructing the Heart orifices
cough with phlegm that is hard to expel
abscesses, boils, and breast inflammation (internal and external use)
uso_historico: Recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing as a superior-grade herb, praised for 'strengthening the will' and memory. It is part of classical spirit-calming formulas such as Tian Wang Bu Xin Dan and Gui Pi Tang.
precauciones: Contraindicated in Yin deficiency with Heat; use with caution with Phlegm-Heat. It irritates the stomach lining: avoid with ulcers or gastritis; high doses may cause nausea and vomiting. Avoid high doses during pregnancy.
nota: American Dragon lists the Heart and Lung meridians (and sometimes the Liver); many materia medica texts, including Bensky, also include the Kidney.

latin: Alisma orientale (Sam.) Juz. / Alisma plantago-aquatica (Alismatis Rhizoma)
acciones: drains Damp-Heat from the Lower Jiao
indicaciones_tradicionales: difficult urination and urinary retention
edema
diarrhea due to Dampness
painful urination due to Damp-Heat (lin syndrome)
vaginal discharge due to Damp-Heat
dizziness and vertigo due to Phlegm-Dampness or fluid retention
spermatorrhea due to Kidney Fire with Yin deficiency
uso_historico: Recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing. It is a component of classical formulas such as Liu Wei Di Huang Wan and Wu Ling San, and was used as an aid in the 'wasting and thirst' disorder (xiao ke).
precauciones: Use with caution in sinking Spleen Qi and in spermatorrhea or discharge due to Kidney Yang deficiency or Cold-Dampness. Avoid simultaneous use with pharmaceutical diuretics. Excessive use may cause gastrointestinal discomfort.

acciones: regulates Qi and clears the Middle Jiao
moves stagnant Qi and reduces distension
indicaciones_tradicionales: abdominal distension and a feeling of fullness
chest tightness and hypochondriac pain due to Qi stagnation
indigestion with food retention
nausea due to Qi stagnation
accumulation of Phlegm and fluids
prolapse of the uterus, rectum, or stomach
uso_historico: It was formally distinguished from zhi shi in the Kai Bao Ben Cao (Song dynasty). It is gentler than zhi shi and is used mainly to move Qi in the chest and diaphragm.
precauciones: Use caution or avoid during pregnancy; use with caution in Spleen and Stomach deficiency and avoid prolonged use. Contains p-synephrine (a stimulant structurally related to ephedrine); data on its effect on blood pressure and heart rate are conflicting, and cardiovascular events have been reported with multi-ingredient supplements. It may not be safe during breastfeeding (NCCIH).
nota: 'Aurantium peel' is ambiguous: it was interpreted as zhi ke (Aurantii Fructus, the nearly ripe fruit of Citrus aurantium, used mainly for its thick peel), distinct from zhi shi (the unripe fruit, listed separately here) and from chen pi (tangerine peel).

acciones: clears Heat and drains Fire from the Qi level, the Lung, and the Stomach
indicaciones_tradicionales: high fever with thirst and restlessness
cough with thick yellow phlegm due to Heat in the Lung
dry cough due to Yin deficiency
night sweats and afternoon fever due to Yin deficiency ('steaming bones')
intense thirst and wasting (xiao ke, diabetes)
mouth ulcers due to Stomach Fire
excessive sexual desire due to Kidney Fire
uso_historico: Recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing. It is part of the classical formula Bai Hu Tang (with shi gao) for Heat at the Qi level and of Zhi Bai Di Huang Wan for Fire due to Yin deficiency.
precauciones: Contraindicated in diarrhea, in Spleen and Stomach deficiency with Cold, and in Kidney Yang deficiency. Use caution with insulin or blood-sugar-lowering drugs because of a possible synergistic effect (hypoglycemia).

acciones: breaks up Qi stagnation and reduces accumulations
descends Qi and unblocks the intestines
indicaciones_tradicionales: epigastric or abdominal distension and pain due to Qi stagnation
indigestion and food retention
constipation with abdominal distension
diarrhea or dysentery with tenesmus due to accumulation
chest tightness due to turbid Phlegm
organ prolapse (uterus, rectum, stomach) at high doses
uso_historico: It appears in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing. It is a key ingredient in purgative and Qi-regulating formulas such as Da Cheng Qi Tang, Zhi Zhu Wan, and Si Ni San.
precauciones: Use with caution during pregnancy, in Qi weakness, in Stomach deficiency with Cold, and with gastric or peptic ulcers. May interact with diuretics. Contains p-synephrine (see NCCIH warnings on bitter orange).
nota: The names 'chih-shih fruit' and 'zhishi fruit' refer to the same herb (zhi shi).
etiquetas: chih-shih fruit / zhishi fruit (one herb: zhi shi)

acciones: clears Heat and drains Fire, relieving irritability
cools the Blood and stops bleeding
resolves toxicity and reduces swelling (external use)
indicaciones_tradicionales: fever with irritability, restlessness, and insomnia
chest tightness and irritability due to Heat
jaundice due to Damp-Heat
painful urination due to Damp-Heat
nosebleeds, vomiting of blood, and blood in the urine due to Heat in the Blood
red, painful eyes due to Liver Fire
mouth ulcers
sprains and traumatic swelling (poultice)
uso_historico: Recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing. It is classically used in Zhi Zi Chi Tang (Shang Han Lun) for irritability and insomnia due to Heat and in Yin Chen Hao Tang for jaundice.
precauciones: Contraindicated in soft stools or poor appetite due to Spleen and Stomach deficiency-Cold. Avoid in Heat due to Blood deficiency. May enhance the effect of sedatives. Prolonged use of high doses has been associated with mesenteric fibrosis (mesenteric phlebosclerosis).

latin: Phyllostachys nigra var. henonis / Bambusa spp. (Bambusae Succus)
parte: sap obtained by heating fresh stems
acciones: unblocks the Heart orifices obstructed by Phlegm and penetrates the channels
indicaciones_tradicionales: cough with thick yellow phlegm due to Phlegm-Heat in the Lung
loss of consciousness due to Phlegm obstructing the Heart orifices
Wind-stroke (apoplexy) with Phlegm
paralysis or numbness of the limbs due to Phlegm in the channels
childhood convulsions due to Phlegm-Heat
mania and mental disorders due to Phlegm-Heat
uso_historico: Recorded in the Ming Yi Bie Lu. It was traditionally taken on its own as a juice or mixed with ginger juice to moderate its cold nature, especially in apoplexy with Phlegm.
precauciones: Contraindicated in cough due to Cold, in soft stools due to Spleen deficiency, and in Cold Phlegm or Phlegm-Dampness.

indicaciones_tradicionales: edema
scanty urination
turbid, painful urination
watery diarrhea
vaginal discharge due to Dampness
jaundice due to Damp-Heat
uso_historico: Recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing as a middle-grade herb. It is a component of the classical formulas Wu Ling San and Zhu Ling Tang from the Shang Han Lun for fluid retention.
precauciones: Do not use when Dampness is not present. Prolonged use may damage Yin. May enhance the effect of diuretics and electrolyte loss.
nota: American Dragon describes it as slightly cool/neutral; most sources list it as neutral.

acciones: releases the exterior and disperses Wind-Cold
moves Qi and harmonizes the Middle Jiao
indicaciones_tradicionales: Wind-Cold common cold with chills, fever, and congestion
cough with chest tightness due to Wind-Cold
nausea and vomiting due to Qi stagnation in the Middle Jiao
epigastric distension and poor appetite
nausea during pregnancy and restless fetus
poisoning or digestive upset from fish or shellfish
uso_historico: First appears in the Ming Yi Bie Lu (compiled by Tao Hongjing). It is used in formulas such as Xiang Su San for colds with Qi stagnation and as a traditional antidote for fish and shellfish.
precauciones: Avoid in Wind-Heat patterns, Yin deficiency with fever, Qi deficiency with spontaneous sweating, and vomiting due to Stomach Fire. Excessive and prolonged use may deplete Qi.

latin: Aster tataricus L. f. (Asteris Radix et Rhizoma)
categoria_mtc: transforms Phlegm and stops cough (relieves cough and shortness of breath)
acciones: moistens the Lung and descends Qi
indicaciones_tradicionales: cough with phlegm due to Wind-Cold
chronic cough due to Lung deficiency
cough with abundant phlegm that is hard to expel
cough with blood-streaked sputum
shortness of breath and wheezing (asthma)
rebellious rising of Lung Qi
uso_historico: Recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing. It has been used for cough of almost any origin, and the honey-prepared form is preferred for Dryness or Lung Yin deficiency.
precauciones: Use with caution in cough due to Yin deficiency with Heat and in excess Heat; avoid prolonged use or high doses.
